explain.say: Have you heard that a new habit takes 21 days? Scientists tested it, and the real answer is more surprising. Look at the graph. Along the bottom are days of repeating something, and up the side is how automatic it feels, which means how much it happens without you thinking.

explain.say: See day 66 on average? In a 2009 study in London, Phillippa Lally found people took 66 days on average to make a habit automatic. But it ranged from 18 to 254 days, depending on the person and the habit! Why might flossing take longer than drinking water?

faq.a: A habit is something you do so often, in the same situation, that it happens almost automatically, like brushing your teeth before bed.

faq.q: Why is a new habit hard at first?
faq.a: At the start, your brain has not linked the situation and the action yet, so you need to remember and choose it every time. That takes effort and willpower.
asks: Why is starting a habit so hard?

faq.a: Each repeat in the same place or time strengthens the link in your brain between the cue and the action. Soon the cue alone starts the habit.
asks: How do I make a habit stick?

faq.q: How many days does it take to form a habit?
faq.a: In Phillippa Lally's 2009 study, it took 66 days on average, but anywhere from 18 to 254 days. The popular 21-day idea is a myth; simple habits form faster than hard ones.
asks: Tell me about day 66 on average
Is it 21 days to form a habit?

faq.q: What happens when a habit becomes automatic?
faq.a: You do it without having to think or decide, almost on autopilot. The study found missing a single day did not undo progress, so do not give up after a slip.
asks: What if I miss a day?

facts: Lally and colleagues at University College London (published 2009/2010) found habits took a median of 66 days to reach automaticity, with a range of 18 to 254 days.
The "21 days" idea is often traced to surgeon Maxwell Maltz's 1960 book, which said it takes a minimum of about 21 days to adjust to change.

quiz.say: On average, how many days did Lally's study find it took to form a habit?
quiz.show: Average days to form a habit in the study
quiz.why: The average was 66 days, with a range of 18 to 254.

wrong.0: A week was far too short for almost everyone.
wrong.1: 21 days is a popular myth, not what the study found.

quiz.say: Ravi misses one day of his new reading habit. What does the research say?
quiz.why: The study found missing a single day did not seriously harm habit building.

wrong.0: One slip did not ruin progress in the study.
wrong.2: There is no need to restart; just carry on.
